title: Los Angeles weather: Storm expected to bring heavy rain, flood risk to Southern California. Here's the timeline - ABC7 Los Angeles
text:
Los Angeles weather: As storm moves out of SoCal, expect dry and cool conditions - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Weather 
 As storm moves out of SoCal, expect dry and cool conditions 
 A powerful cold front delivered as advertised Thursday, dumping heavy rain on much of the Southland as the morning commute unfolded. Conditions are expected to turn dry and cool Friday and Saturday, with highs mainly in the 60s at lower elevations. Friday, November 20, 2026 5:54AM Share Follow ABC7 on Google Este artículo se ofrece en Español LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- A powerful cold front delivered as advertised Thursday, dumping heavy rain on much of the Southland as the morning commute unfolded, leading to pockets of flooding that made driving treacherous and isolated mud flows in some areas before the storm quickly moved to the east.
 The rain prompted various flood advisories and severe thunderstorm warnings for a large swath of the Southland stretching from Mount Wilson to Pasadena to downtown to Santa Monica to Long Beach and Rolling Hills.
 The Los Angeles County Department of Public Health issued an ocean water quality rain advisory for all county beaches, warning people to avoid water contact until at least noon Monday because runoff can raise bacteria levels. The agency especially urged people to stay out of the water near storm drains, creeks and rivers, where runoff can carry bacteria, chemicals, debris, trash and other hazards into the ocean and onto beach sand.
 A High Surf Advisory is in effect for Los Angeles County beaches through 9 a.m. Friday, with large surf, dangerous rip currents and hazardous conditions on jetties expected. Forecasters said the high tide could potentially send seawater over low-lying beaches, walkways and parking lots and causing beach erosion.
 Conditions are expected to turn dry and cool Friday and Saturday, with highs mainly in the 60s at lower elevations.
 A weaker storm system could bring a slight chance of rain to Los Angeles and Orange counties Sunday night or Monday.
 Friday forecast
 Los Angeles and Orange counties Friday can expect a 10% probability of morning showers, along with a high of 64 degrees and a low of 44.
 The valleys and Inland Empire Friday will see a high of 64 degrees and a low of 40, along with a 10% probability of showers in the morning.
 Beach communities Friday can expect a high of 66 degrees and a low of 50. There is a 20% chance of showers.
 Mountain communities will see a high of 42 degrees and a chilly overnight low of 17 Friday. There is a 50% chance of rain, with snow falling at elevations above 6,500 feet.
 Desert areas can expect partly sunny conditions with a high of 57 and a low of 25 Friday, with Palm Springs reaching a high of 71.
 City News Service contributed to this report.
